### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5b22ee759364cb675ff5d4281b797c3684323f69`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5b22ee759364cb675ff5d4281b797c3684323f69` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fe2a71e4e06127134d7215f4f86bdfe500bc73b5` — the merge of head `868cfd7e797dc67a17f7a7f4df224edf047da3be` into base `5b22ee759364cb675ff5d4281b797c3684323f69`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fe2a71e4e06127134d7215f4f86bdfe500bc73b5 && git checkout fe2a71e4e06127134d7215f4f86bdfe500bc73b5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5b22ee759364cb675ff5d4281b797c3684323f69 868cfd7e797dc67a17f7a7f4df224edf047da3be && git checkout -B drift-repro 5b22ee759364cb675ff5d4281b797c3684323f69 && git merge --no-ff 868cfd7e797dc67a17f7a7f4df224edf047da3be

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5b22ee759364cb675ff5d4281b797c3684323f69
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5b22ee759364cb675ff5d4281b797c3684323f69` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `81072e50e85a4f02ed801b5e25d316cf103b07ad`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-proxy-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-proxy-catalog-facets.test.ts + packages/spec/src/marketplace/marketplace.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/marketplace/taxonomy.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.marketplace-category-retired.ts, packages/rest/src/query-multiplicity.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-public-url.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-proxy-browse-only.test.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/marketplaceApi.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/marketplaceTaxonomy.ts

Inputs read: card #31173 (body, triage 6709309123, claim 6710538394, os-dev-report 6711774130), PR #31234 (body, 3-file list, net diff `origin/main...81072e50`), the head's check-runs. `.changeset/31173-marketplace-catalog-facet-filters.md` is a prose face: read for ②, not reviewed. Check-runs on the head at review time: 27 success, 13 skipped, 6 still `in_progress` (Test Core 1–5/8, Type Check · workspace), none failed; the gate verdicts that are in do not move the verdict below, and the pending six cannot turn a ④ must-fix into a PASS.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies at `GET|HEAD /api/v1/marketplace/packages`, judged against the published spec on `main` (`MarketplaceSearchRequestSchema`, `taxonomy.zod.ts`) and the cited code:

1. **Facet keys honoured — `businessFunctions`, `industries`, `solutionTypes` (one comma-separated value each) and `maturity` (one value).** Right. They are the keys the published request schema declares (`marketplace.zod.ts:434–442`); the allowed values are read from the spec enums' `.options`, not copied; OR inside a facet and AND across matches the schema's own docblock ("Values inside one facet are OR-ed, facets are AND-ed"). The comma form is the platform's wire spelling of a list-valued query parameter (`fields`, `names`), not a new capability, so the accept set widens nowhere.
2. **Undeclared value refused, 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`.** Right. The spec's `z.enum` refuses the same value; the code is the ledger's standard 400 code (ADR-0112). Case-sensitive (`Retail` refused) matches the enums.
3. **Repeated key refused (`?industries=a&industries=b`), shared `repeatedQueryParamMessage`.** Right, as a declared narrowing. The spec declares an array, not its query encoding; the comma form carries every declared array, so no declared value is lost, and the refusal is the repo's one multiplicity rule (`query-multiplicity.ts`, #6877) applied as that file prescribes for a non-`res` door (message only, own envelope).
4. **Empty facet refused (`?solutionTypes=`, `?solutionTypes=,`).** Right, with a note. The spec's `z.array(...).optional()` admits `[]`, which as an "any of these" filter matches nothing; refusing it narrows a shape no consumer can use and the `(narrowing)` arm covers it.
5. **`?category=` is no longer a filter and is silently ignored (200, whole snapshot).** WRONG — see ④ must-fix. The spec does not merely "not declare" `category`: it declares it as a tombstone whose parse refuses any value with `retiredCategoryGuidance('MarketplaceSearchRequest.category')`, and the spec's own migration entry (`18.marketplace-category-retired.ts`, acceptanceCriteria) states that a `MarketplaceSearchRequestSchema` parse "refuses it with its prescription". The proxy turns that loud refusal into a silent strip. The accept set for `category` did not widen (it was accepted before), so this does not flip Clause-②; it leaves the declared narrowing half done.
6. **Every other unknown key, `solutionType` (singular, the card's spelling) included, is ignored.** Unchanged pre-existing posture (measured by the dev: the proxy refused no query parameter before). Noted in ④ as should-fix, not a contract break.
7. **Server-side paging over the filtered set; `total` counts every match; `limit` 1–100 default 50.** Right, and it is the card's expected item 1 on the snapshot path. `?limit=abc` → NaN → empty page is pre-existing and out of this card.
8. **Row defaults — absent/undeclared `solution_type` reads as `app`, absent/undeclared `maturity` as `stable`.** Right: the listing schema's `.default('app')` / `.default('stable')`, and the console's `effectiveSolutionType` (`marketplaceTaxonomy.ts:95–97`) reads the row the same way, so the server and the first consumer agree.
9. **Rows without the taxonomy columns pass no business-function or industry filter.** Right (`listColumn` → `[]`); matches #31011's plan that those facets return nothing until cloud#3661 serves the columns.
10. **Cloud path: facets validated in the handler, then `pathname + search` forwarded verbatim; the LRU cache key already includes `search`.** Right as far as this repo goes; what the cloud does with the names is unmeasured — escalated in ③.
11. **Public surface of `@objectstack/cloud-connection`: no export, type or error code added; new imports (`@objectstack/spec/marketplace` taxonomy symbols, `@objectstack/rest` `repeatedQueryParamMessage`) are existing workspace dependencies and the spec subpath exists in `exports`.** Right.
12. **HEAD: the refusal applies to HEAD as to GET; a filtered HEAD answers headers with no body.** Right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31173-marketplace-catalog-facet-filters.md`: `'@objectstack/cloud-connection': patch`, title `feat(cloud-connection)!:`, BREAKING banner with Before/Now/Who moves/The remedy, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

- **Level fits.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3: the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone; a query parameter of a served route is not something a metadata author writes, so `none` → `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". The `fixed` group bumps the family together either way. Check Changeset and the ADR-0087 gate (PR-automation) are green on this head.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` holds.** The proxy accepts nothing the spec does not declare: the four keys and their vocabularies are the schema's; the comma encoding is the platform's spelling of a declared array; `q` / `limit` / `offset` pre-exist this diff. What it refuses (items 2–4) and what it stops honouring (item 5) only shrink the accept set, so the arm is `(narrowing)`, not `yes`. The declaration is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body, as the face requires.
- **ADR-0087 disposition.** `no-migration-prescription` is honest in the ADR's sense: nothing at rest carries a catalog query, so `os migrate meta` has no seam; the changeset's "remedy" paragraph is a request-rewrite note, not a metadata migration prescription, and the gate accepted the pairing on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (PR "Acceptance notes" and os-dev-report 6711774130); `open_questions: []`.

1. **`solutionTypes` (spec) implemented where the card wrote `solutionType`.** Accepted. The published schema is the contract and it declares the plural list; `solutionType` is the listing's own key. The card's spelling is a drafting slip; the `domain:ui` follow-up card must carry `solutionTypes` verbatim.
2. **One comma-separated value per facet; repeated key / empty facet / undeclared value refused 400 before both paths — covered by the spec?** Answered in ① items 1–4: the undeclared-value refusal is the spec's own; the repeated-key and empty-facet refusals are narrowings of encodings the spec does not declare, properly under the `(narrowing)` arm; nothing is accepted that the spec does not declare, so Clause-② stays `no`.
3. **`?category=` ignored, not refused.** NOT accepted — must-fix in ④. The spec's `retiredKey` tombstone and its migration entry declare a loud refusal with the prescription; the card's "retired (no second spelling kept)" is satisfied on the spelling side but the spec's refusal is not made real.
4. **Cloud path forwards the query verbatim; cloud handling NOT MEASURED.** Escalated, not a fix here: on the default configuration (no `OS_MARKETPLACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, `resolveMarketplacePublicBaseUrl` → `''`) every list request takes the cloud path, so the card's "paginates server side" is delivered only where the snapshot path is configured, and a cloud that ignores the names answers an unfiltered 200 after the proxy has validated the facets. A card on objectstack-ai/cloud (pairing with cloud#3661) must pin the same names, the comma encoding and `solutionTypes` plural; the seat files it at landing beside the `domain:ui` card.
5. **Body claim not on the tree.** The PR body and the dev report say the console client `listMarketplacePackages` "still accepts a `category` argument no caller passes". On `main` its signature is `{ q?, limit?, offset? }` (`marketplaceApi.ts:252`); the `category` at `:902` is `OrgPackageSummary`, the org catalog, not the marketplace list. Prose only, but the `domain:ui` follow-up must not be filed on that sentence.
6. **Test placement.** The new suite copies `captureHandler` and `fakeCtx` byte-for-byte from `marketplace-proxy-browse-only.test.ts`, the component's existing harness file; ruling record 6583487846 puts a new pin for a component with a shared harness file into that file as a top-level `describe`. Should-fix in ④.
7. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay) — no out-of-relay login to name.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing itself, read against the published spec on `main` and the cited code. Two questions: does it take a declared capability away at the consumer, and does it make the spec's own refusal real?

**Taken away at the consumer?** No. Every capability the request schema declares for the four keys is delivered on the snapshot path (OR/AND, vocabularies, maturity, paging over the filtered set) and forwarded on the cloud path; what the proxy stops honouring, `category`, the spec itself retired in 18. Nothing declared is narrowed away.

**The spec's own refusal made real?** Only partly, and that is the failing half.

- **MUST-FIX — `?category=` is silently ignored where the spec declares a loud refusal.** `MarketplaceSearchRequestSchema.category` is `retiredKey(retiredCategoryGuidance('MarketplaceSearchRequest.category'))`: `z.never` with the prescription as its error, built — per `retired-key.ts`'s own docblock — exactly so that a removal is audible and never a "silent strip". The spec's migration entry `18.marketplace-category-retired.ts` states the acceptance criterion in words: a `MarketplaceSearchRequestSchema` parse "refuses it with its prescription". The proxy is the one in-repo door that reads a search request's query; after this diff a client sending `?category=crm` receives 200 and the whole catalog. That is the card's own "silently dead" failure reproduced by design, and it contradicts the diff's own reasoning one function up: a misspelled facet value is refused because "an empty page would hide a misspelling", yet a dead filter key is let through because a full page hides it just as well. The repo's multiplicity doctrine the diff cites says the same: a wrong answer delivered as a success is the shape to refuse. Fix: in `readCatalogListQuery`, `params.has('category')` → `{ ok: false, param: 'category', message: retiredCategoryGuidance('MarketplaceSearchRequest.category') }` (the spec's prescription, byte-for-byte, already exported from `@objectstack/spec/marketplace`), answered as the other refusals are, 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, before both paths; retarget the two `?category=` tests (served whole / narrows nothing beside a filter) to the refusal and keep the ablation anchor. The changeset's Now paragraph then reads "refused with the spec's prescription" instead of "ignored". This is a FAIL.
- **Should-fix — the card's spelling `solutionType` (singular) is swallowed silently.** The card, the console's `FacetSelection.solutionType` and the listing key all spell it singular; a follow-up author will send `?solutionType=template` and get the whole catalog with 200. Either refuse the known-wrong key naming `solutionTypes` (one more row in the read, the same envelope), or at minimum file the `domain:ui` card with the plural spelled out; the first is the design that holds without relying on the card text.
- **Should-fix — harness duplication.** Move the 13 pins into `marketplace-proxy-browse-only.test.ts` as top-level `describe`s, or lift `captureHandler` / `fakeCtx` into one shared helper both files import (ruling record 6583487846).
- **Should-fix — prose on the tree.** Strike the "`listMarketplacePackages` still accepts a `category` argument" sentence from the PR body (③.5).
- **Escalate — cloud path.** As ③.4: a cloud card must adopt the names and encoding; until it does, the default configuration validates and then trusts the cloud.

Everything else tried holds: repeated/blank/undeclared values on each key, `?category=` beside a real filter, HEAD on both paths, offset past the end, a row with an undeclared `solution_type` string (read as `app`, as the console reads it), the cache key carrying the facets, and the fetch-free refusal on the cloud-only configuration.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-eqgsby`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5o8PE7ZtVjcor51wBZ (fable subagent)`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `868cfd7e797dc67a17f7a7f4df224edf047da3be`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-proxy-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-proxy-browse-only.test.ts + packages/spec/src/marketplace/marketplace.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/marketplace/taxonomy.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.marketplace-category-retired.ts, packages/rest/src/query-multiplicity.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-public-url.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/marketplaceApi.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/marketplaceTaxonomy.ts

Delta review of the rework after record 6711888512 (FAIL on head `81072e50`), by the same reviewer; a full record on the new head. Inputs: card #31173 (body, triage 6709309123, claim 6710538394, os-dev-reports 6711774130 and 6712663916), PR #31234 (patched body v2, 3-file list, net diff `origin/main...868cfd7e`, and the delta `81072e50..868cfd7e`), the head's check-runs. The changeset is a prose face: read for ②, not reviewed. Check-runs on `868cfd7e` at the time of writing: 37 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending (a second Check Changeset run, started by the body edit, finished green while this record was written). Cited code did not move: the spec marketplace files, `retired-key.ts`, the migration entry, `query-multiplicity.ts`, `marketplace-public-url.ts` and the two console files are byte-identical between the round-1 `main` (`714dda8f`) and this head.

**The head's two commits.** `248a01c7` merges `origin/main` (`733efbd4`) once: `git show --cc 248a01c7` prints no hunk for any path in scope, and `git diff 733efbd4 248a01c7` on the scope files equals the round-1 content exactly, so the merge resolved nothing by hand and carried nothing of its own. `868cfd7e` is the rework; the net diff against `main` is the same three paths as before, with the separate test file gone and its pins in the harness file.

### ① Derived judgments

Round-1 items 1–4 and 7–12 stand unchanged (the delta touches none of their code): facet keys and vocabularies from the published schema, OR within / AND across, undeclared-value refusal, repeated-key and empty-facet refusals as declared narrowings, server paging over the filtered set, `app` / `stable` row defaults agreeing with the console's `effectiveSolutionType`, rows without the columns passing no facet, cloud path forwarding after the read, no export / type / error code added, HEAD handled as GET. Re-judged on the delta:

5. **`?category=` is refused 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, before both paths, with the spec's prescription.** Right now. `readCatalogListQuery` opens with `params.has('category')` and answers `Query parameter 'category' is retired: ` followed by `retiredCategoryGuidance('MarketplaceSearchRequest.category')` byte-for-byte (imported from `@objectstack/spec/marketplace`, where `taxonomy.zod.ts` exports it and the schema's tombstone uses the same call). This is the refusal `retired-key.ts` and the migration entry `18.marketplace-category-retired.ts` ("a parse of MarketplaceSearchRequestSchema refuses it with its prescription") declare, made real at the one in-repo door that reads a search request's query. `has` refuses the bare key too (`?category=`), which is right: the key is retired, not a value of it. The read sits ahead of the R2 and cloud branches, so the pins' `fetchCalls` is empty on both configurations. The card's "retired (no second spelling kept)" is now met on both sides. The accept set only shrinks further: no Clause-② movement.
13. **Pins moved into `marketplace-proxy-browse-only.test.ts`.** Right: they use the file's `captureHandler` / `fakeCtx(method, path)`; the module-level `beforeEach` fetch stub now also wraps the three existing pins, which make no fetch, so nothing they measure changes. 3 + 13 pins; the two `?category=` pins assert the 400, the code, the prescription substring and no fetch, alone and beside a real filter and on the cloud-only configuration.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged frontmatter: `'@objectstack/cloud-connection': patch`, `feat(cloud-connection)!:`, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line-initial in the changeset and the PR body, `Metadata-protocol: none`, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The rework reworded the narrowing clause ("refusing the retired `?category=` filter"), the marker's why ("refuses one the spec already retired, with the spec's own prescription") and the Now / Who-moves paragraphs ("A script still sending `?category=` gets the 400 instead of a filtered list"), so the prose now describes the tree.

- **Level fits.** A query parameter of a served route is not metadata an author writes: `Metadata-protocol: none` → `patch`; AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3 has a non-protocol breaking change ship `patch` with its banner and ADR-0087 disposition. Check Changeset (both runs) and the ADR-0087 gate are green on this head.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` holds.** Nothing is accepted that the spec does not declare; the delta adds a refusal and removes nothing declared.
- **ADR-0087 disposition** stays honest: nothing at rest records a catalog query, the "remedy" is a request rewrite, not a metadata migration, and the gate accepted the pairing.

### ③ Boundary flags

Round-1 flags and the rework report (os-dev-report 6712663916; `open_questions: []`):

1. **Must-fix `?category=`** — taken, as ① item 5; ablation A1 reported red-first on both retargeted pins. Closed.
2. **Should-fix harness duplication** — taken: the separate file is deleted, the pins are top-level `describe`s in the component's harness file (ruling record 6583487846). Closed.
3. **Should-fix prose on the tree** — taken: the PR body no longer names `listMarketplacePackages` (0 matches); the "Kept as before" note now carries only the pre-existing `?limit=abc` reading. Closed.
4. **Should-fix `?solutionType=` (singular) swallowed** — left as it was, by the seat's call, with the `domain:ui` follow-up to spell `solutionTypes`. Accepted as a seat decision: it is pre-existing posture (the door ignored every unknown key before), not a contract break; it stays a should-fix for the follow-up, see ④.
5. **Cloud path forwards the validated query verbatim; cloud handling NOT MEASURED** — unchanged; escalation stands: a card on objectstack-ai/cloud (pairing with cloud#3661) must pin the same names, comma encoding and plural `solutionTypes`; until then the default configuration (no `OS_MARKETPLACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`) validates and forwards, and the card's server-side paging is delivered where the snapshot path is configured.
6. **Dev deviation: the PR body was patched by the seat, not the dev** (os-dev.md single-writer rule); the body read here is the seat's v2 and matches the tree. Noted, no action.
7. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay) — no out-of-relay login to name.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`, over the floor (the plugin and the harness file) with the cited code read.

**Taken away at the consumer?** No. Every capability the request schema declares for `businessFunctions`, `industries`, `solutionTypes` and `maturity` is delivered on the snapshot path and forwarded on the cloud path; `category` is what the spec retired, and the diff removes only that.

**The spec's own refusal made real?** Yes, now on both sides. The three refusals the spec implies (undeclared value: the enum; `category`: the tombstone's prescription) and the two the `(narrowing)` arm declares (repeated key, empty facet) all answer 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` before either path, with messages naming the parameter and the remedy; a caller still filtering by category reads the spec's own sentence instead of receiving the whole catalog as though it had matched. The round-1 inconsistency (a misspelled value refused, a dead key let through) is gone.

Probed on the new head and holding: `?category=` alone, blank, beside a real filter, on the cloud-only configuration (no fetch); the prescription substring is the exported text, not a copy; repeated / blank / undeclared values on each key; `q` plus paging with `total` over the filtered set; HEAD on both paths; a row with an undeclared `solution_type` string read as `app`, as the console reads it; the module-level fetch stub against the three pre-existing pins.

- **Should-fix (carried, not blocking):** `?solutionType=` singular — the card's, the console `FacetSelection`'s and the listing key's spelling — is ignored and answers the whole catalog with 200; one more row in `readCatalogListQuery` naming `solutionTypes` would hold without relying on the follow-up card's text. The seat's decision to carry it in the `domain:ui` card is accepted.
- **Escalate (carried):** the cloud list route, as ③.5.

No must-fix.
